chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'We narrate and say: Whoever prays while sitting without an excuse, his prayer is two rak'ahs with one ruku' and two prostrations with one sajdah.' He said, 'It is not so; it is complete for you.'
ai.seo_question: Is the prayer of someone sitting without a valid excuse considered valid and complete or deficient in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevalent view that praying while seated without a valid excuse results in a deficient, half-measure prayer. He clarifies that such a prayer is considered complete (*tammah*) and fully valid, emphasizing the principle of ease (*rukhas*) in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the Shia position that the default validity of acts of worship is preserved unless explicitly abrogated, distinguishing it from some Sunni schools that may view it as a lesser form of prayer.
